defects.description: The spend guard uses strict `>` instead of `>=`, so a request whose cost exactly equals the tokens on hand is rejected even though the bucket holds enough to cover it.
paraphrases: A bucket holding precisely `cost` tokens should permit the spend, yet the strict-greater-than test turns that exact-balance case into a denial.
The last available token can never be spent in one call: when the level equals the requested amount the affordability check fails and the decision comes back not-allowed.
Callers asking for exactly the number of tokens currently present are wrongly told to wait, because equality is excluded from the sufficiency comparison.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '            if bucket.level >= cost:'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: The lazy refill subtracts the accrued tokens instead of adding them, so an idle bucket drains over time and eventually goes negative rather than replenishing toward its ceiling.
paraphrases: Elapsed time is meant to credit the bucket, but the replenishment line deducts the amount earned, so keys grow more throttled the longer they sit quiet.
The sign on the time-based top-up is inverted, turning the refill routine into a slow leak that drives levels below zero.
Rather than raising the balance by the tokens accumulated since the last touch, the code removes them, so an untouched bucket loses capacity instead of recovering it.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '            bucket.level = min(bucket.burst, bucket.level + gained)'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: When no explicit burst is supplied the per-key ceiling defaults to the minimum of the new capacity and the limiter's burst instead of the maximum, so raising a key's capacity above the limiter-wide burst yields a ceiling below capacity and trips the 'burst must be >= capacity' validation.
paraphrases: The omitted-burst fallback collapses to whichever of the requested capacity and the global burst is smaller, so a per-key override that increases capacity beyond that burst is rejected with a ValueError.
Because the default headroom picks the lesser of the two ceilings, a key can be assigned a cap that exceeds its own top, breaking the invariant checked on the very next line.
Configuring a key to a larger capacity than the limiter's burst should widen its bucket, but the min() makes the ceiling fall beneath capacity and the call fails validation instead.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        top = float(burst) if burst is not None else max(cap, self._burst)'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.

defects.description: The constructor rejects `refill_per_sec == 0` via `<= 0`, even though a zero refill rate is documented as valid (a static bucket that never replenishes), so a legitimate non-negative configuration raises ValueError.
paraphrases: A refill rate of exactly zero denotes a bucket that only ever drains and should be accepted, but the boundary treats it as an illegal value.
The guard bars the zero case together with the negatives, making it impossible to build a never-replenishing limiter despite the documented non-negative contract.
By flagging a zero rate the check over-tightens the input to strictly positive values, contradicting the stated allowance for any non-negative rate.
defects.rationale: Correct form: '        if refill_per_sec < 0:'. LLM-seeded; human R/F/U-audited & confirmed 2026-07-12.
